I couldn't open any files, so this diagnosis comes from the file list and the usual layout of this NestJS boilerplate. I haven't confirmed it against the code, and the line ranges are estimates.

The likeliest cause is in the persistence layer's `update` method. A 200 response with unchanged values means the save call ran but wrote the old data back. In this boilerplate, `update` loads the existing entity, merges the payload into it, and saves the result. If the merge order is reversed (existing data spread over the payload), or if the mapper's `toPersistence` drops the name and role fields, the old values are saved again. The response and the database would then both show the original values.

The next two places to check are `UsersService.update`, which may build the payload from the existing user instead of the DTO, and `UsersController.update`, which may pass the wrong id or the wrong DTO.

candidates.explanation: The update method merges the payload with the existing entity and saves it. If the merge order is wrong (existing domain data spread over the payload) or the mapper discards the changed fields, the old values are saved. The call then succeeds with 200 but writes nothing new, and the returned user shows the original name and role.

The service prepares the payload (clears fields, resolves role, status, photo and email) before calling the repository. If it passes the existing user or a stale or partial object instead of the DTO values, the repository is called with unchanged name and role. The call succeeds but changes nothing.
The PATCH handler may pass the wrong id or the wrong DTO to the service, for example the original or an empty payload. The result would be a normal 200 response with unchanged data.

fix.description: In update(), merge so that the payload overrides the existing data: UserMapper.toPersistence({ ...UserMapper.toDomain(entity), ...payload }). Make sure the mapper copies name and role to the persistence entity. Then check that UsersService.update passes the DTO values through to the repository.
